subject: Hospitality
title: Kemmons Wilson: Holiday Inn's Founder
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Kemmons Wilson: Holiday Inn's Founder.

hook.text: Kemmons Wilson took a family road trip in 1951 and hated every motel. So he built his own chain: Holiday Inn.

buildup.text: He wanted consistency: clean rooms, free parking, kids stay free, no surprises. The same experience in Memphis or Miami.

discovery.text: Wilson franchised aggressively. By 1972, Holiday Inn was the world's largest hotel chain with 1,400 properties.

twist.text: The 'kids stay free' policy was revolutionary. It made Holiday Inn the family travel brand and expanded the market dramatically.

climax.text: Wilson proved the franchise model could scale hospitality globally. Every chain that followed used his playbook.

punchline.text: A bad road trip inspired a global chain. Frustration built an empire.

quiz.question: What inspired Kemmons Wilson to create Holiday Inn?
options: A frustrating family road trip with terrible motel experiences
